statement: Whenever special_array(nums) returns a result r, let n = len(nums) and for any integer x let C(x) be the number of indices i with 0 <= i < n and nums[i] >= x. Then r is the unique integer x such that 0 <= x <= n and C(x) = x, if such an integer exists; otherwise r = -1. Equivalently, r != -1 if and only if there exists x with 0 <= x <= n and C(x) = x, and when r != -1 we have 0 <= r <= n and C(r) = r.
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 0 <= nums[i] <= 1000.

statement: For every nums satisfying the preconditions, special_array(nums) returns a result r; it does not fail.
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 0 <= nums[i] <= 1000.

statement: Whenever special_array(nums) returns a result r, either r = -1 or 1 <= r <= len(nums).
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 0 <= nums[i] <= 1000.

statement: Whenever special_array(nums) returns a result r with r != -1, the number of indices i with 0 <= i < len(nums) and nums[i] >= r is exactly r.
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 0 <= nums[i] <= 1000.

statement: Whenever special_array(nums) returns a result r with r = -1, for every integer x with 0 <= x <= len(nums), the number of indices i with 0 <= i < len(nums) and nums[i] >= x is not equal to x.
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 0 <= nums[i] <= 1000.

statement: Whenever special_array(nums) returns a result r with r != -1, for every integer y with 0 <= y <= len(nums) and y != r, the number of indices i with 0 <= i < len(nums) and nums[i] >= y is not equal to y.
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 0 <= nums[i] <= 1000.

statement: Whenever special_array(nums) returns a result r with r != -1, let C(x) be the number of indices i with 0 <= i < len(nums) and nums[i] >= x. Then for every integer x with 0 <= x < r, C(x) > x; and for every integer x with r < x <= len(nums), C(x) < x.
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 0 <= nums[i] <= 1000.

statement: Whenever special_array(nums) returns a result r with r != -1, r <= M, where M is the maximum of nums, i.e. M = max({nums[i] | 0 <= i < len(nums)}).
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 0 <= nums[i] <= 1000.

statement: If there exists an integer v with 0 <= v < len(nums) such that nums[i] = v for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), then special_array(nums) returns the result -1.
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 0 <= nums[i] <= 1000.

statement: If nums[i] >= len(nums) for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), then special_array(nums) returns the result len(nums).
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 0 <= nums[i] <= 1000.

statement: Whenever special_array(nums) returns a result r with r = len(nums), every element of nums satisfies nums[i] >= len(nums) for 0 <= i < len(nums).
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 0 <= nums[i] <= 1000.

statement: For every two arrays nums and nums2 satisfying the preconditions, if for every integer v the number of indices i with nums[i] = v equals the number of indices i with nums2[i] = v (equivalently, nums2 is a permutation of nums), then whenever special_array(nums) returns r and special_array(nums2) returns s, we have r = s.
preconditions: For two arrays nums and nums2: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100, 1 <= len(nums2) <= 100, and for every i in the respective index ranges, 0 <= nums[i] <= 1000 and 0 <= nums2[i] <= 1000.

statement: Whenever special_array(nums) returns a result r with r != -1, let C(x) be the number of indices i with 0 <= i < len(nums) and nums[i] >= x. Then r is the least integer x with 0 <= x <= len(nums) for which C(x) <= x.
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 0 <= nums[i] <= 1000.

statement: Whenever special_array(nums) returns a result r with r = -1, let n = len(nums) and C(x) be the number of indices i with 0 <= i < n and nums[i] >= x. Then there exists an integer x with 0 <= x < n such that C(x) > x and C(x+1) < x+1.
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 0 <= nums[i] <= 1000.
